locale.description: This catalogue’s language as a BCP 47 tag (en, fr, zh-Hans or zh-Hant), for the options page’s lang attribute. Not shown.

extensionDescription.message: Save the page you’re reading, or a link, to {app}.
extensionDescription.description: The extension’s description in the browser’s list of extensions. {app} is the product name, which the build fills in; keep it as it is.

commandDescription.description: The keyboard shortcut’s name in the browser’s shortcut settings.

contextMenuTitle.description: The item the extension adds to the right-click menu of a link.

badgeTitle.description: The toolbar button’s tooltip after a save, explaining its ✓ or ! badge.

onlyWebPages.message: Only web pages (http or https) can be saved.

onlyWebLinks.message: Only http and https links can be saved.

notConfigured.message: Open the extension’s options and enter the server URL and an access token.

savedLinkOnly.message: Saved to {app} (link only: the page was too large to send)
savedLinkOnly.description: The page’s HTML was over the server’s limit, so only its address was saved and the server downloads the page itself.

alreadySaved.message: Already in {app}, moved to the top
alreadySaved.description: The article was saved before; saving it again moves it back to the top of the Inbox.

alreadySavedLinkOnly.message: Already in {app}, moved to the top (link only: the page was too large to send)

alreadySavedRefetching.description: The article was saved before, but as a preview, a failure or an empty page, so saving its link again downloads it again.

alreadySavedRefetchingLinkOnly.message: Already in {app}, downloading it again (link only: the page was too large to send)

serverMessageLinkOnly.message: $MESSAGE$ (link only: the page was too large to send)
serverMessageLinkOnly.description: After a save the extension doesn’t have its own words for, as from a newer server.

connected.message: Connected to {app}. You’re ready to save pages.
connected.description: On the options page, when the server URL and the access token work.

unreachable.description: $ERROR$ is the browser’s own description of the network error.

notTheApp.message: Something other than {app} answered at $SERVER$. Check the server URL.
notTheApp.description: A web page, not the app, answered at the server URL.

serverAnswered.description: The server failed without saying why. $STATUS$ is the HTTP status.

errorUnauthorized.message: Missing or invalid access token. Create one in Settings.
errorUnauthorized.description: Settings is the web app’s Settings page: use its name in the web app.

errorTooLarge.message: The page is too large to save.

errorBadRequest.message: Send JSON like {"url": "https://..."}, optionally with "html" and "title".
errorBadRequest.description: The server couldn’t read the request. Keep the JSON as it is.

errorInvalidUrl.message: url must be an absolute http or https URL.
errorInvalidUrl.description: The server didn’t accept the page’s address. “url” is the request’s field.

errorServer.message: Something went wrong while saving. Please try again.

serverUrlHint.message: The address of your {app} web app.

tokenHint.message: Create one in the web app under Settings → Access tokens. It is stored only in this browser.
tokenHint.description: “Settings → Access tokens” is a page of the web app and its section: use their names in the web app.

saveAndCheck.description: The options page’s button: it saves the settings, then checks them with the server.

enterServerUrl.message: Enter the address of your server, such as https://read.example.com.

enterToken.message: Paste an access token from the app’s Settings page (it starts with rl_).

usage.message: Save a page with the toolbar button or <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> (Mac: <kbd>Option</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>). Right-click a link to save just the link. $SHORTCUTS$
usage.description: Text in … is shown as keys and in … as code: keep the tags, around the keys’ names on keyboards in this language. $SHORTCUTS$ is where to change the shortcut, from shortcutsChrome or shortcutsFirefox.

shortcuts.example: You can change the shortcut at chrome://extensions/shortcuts.

shortcutsChrome.message: You can change the shortcut at chrome://extensions/shortcuts.
shortcutsChrome.description: Shown in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers. Keep the <code> tags and the address.

shortcutsFirefox.message: You can change the shortcut in about:addons: choose Manage Extension Shortcuts from the gear menu.
shortcutsFirefox.description: Shown in Firefox. Keep the <code> tags and the address. “Manage Extension Shortcuts” is Firefox’s own menu item: use its name in Firefox in this language.
